title: Decide where a catch-up answer gets its FanoutMessages: the hub stores the MLSMessage, not the fanout
design:
Found 2026-11-25 starting the serving side of bead mimid-1wgh.37.104.3,
after its wire format was settled by mimid-1wgh.37.104.6. It blocks that
serving side. The codec and the two bounds are done and do not depend on
it.

THE GAP. §5 says the answer is "fanouts in hub order, each with its
sequence", which assumes the hub has the fanouts. IT DOES NOT.

* room_event.bytes is "the message exactly as received" -- the
  MLSMessage, not the FanoutMessage. No frank, no timestamp framing,
  no Welcome's ratchet tree.
* The encoded FanoutMessage exists as hub::submit's
  Accepted::fanout_body, which goes to the OUTBOX and is deleted on
  delivery.
* follower_event.bytes is "One FanoutMessage exactly as received", which
  is what catch-up wants -- but it is the provider's FOLLOWER role, and
  it only has a row when the hub fanned out to its own domain.
  hub::state::member_domains is the members' domains plus the sender, so
  A ROOM HUBBED HERE WHOSE MEMBERS ARE ALL REMOTE never delivers to this
  provider and has nothing in that log. Checked, not assumed. So the
  follower log cannot be the source in general, which removes the
  cheapest option.

THE READINGS:

1. KEEP THE FANOUT BODY PER EVENT: a room_event.fanout_bytes column,
   written in the transaction that already writes the event and its
   outbox rows and its sequence.
   For: byte-identical to what was delivered by construction, which is
   the property bead mimid-1wgh.37.104.2's ranges also give -- catch-up
   can only return what was really sent. Keyed directly by the fanout
   sequence catch-up 1 introduced. No new failure mode.
   Against: roughly doubles the hub's stored bytes per message, since
   the MLSMessage sits in both room_event.bytes and the fanout body.
   Bounded by retention (message_retention_secs, 7 days by default), so
   it is a constant factor on a window, not unbounded growth.

2. KEEP ONLY THE FRANK and rebuild the FanoutMessage at serve time from
   accepted_at, kind, bytes and the frank.
   For: about 39 bytes an event instead of a second copy of the message.
   Against: it re-encodes. AGENTS.md says to sign and hash the exact
   bytes as received and never re-encode before verifying, and a
   follower checks the frank over the bytes it is given. A rebuild that
   differs by one byte from what was delivered is a franking failure at
   the follower, and the hub would have no way to know. It also has to
   reproduce a Welcome's ratchet_tree option and a commit's
   externalProposals, which room_event does not keep at all.

3. STORE THE FANOUT INSTEAD OF THE MLSMessage: room_event.bytes becomes
   the FanoutMessage and the MLSMessage is read out of it where needed.
   For: no duplication.
   Against: changes what the hub's log holds for every existing reader
   (store::retention, the catch-up window, anything that replays), and
   the hub does need the bare MLSMessage for its own checks.

MY READ, not a decision: reading 1. The duplication is a constant factor
on a retention window that the operator already sets, and byte-identity
is the property catch-up exists to provide. Reading 2 trades a storage
saving for a failure that surfaces at the other end as a franking error,
which is the worst place for it.

WORTH NOTING FOR THE DRAFT: whichever is chosen, §5 should say that a
hub serving catch-up has to keep the fanout as delivered, not merely the
message. The note does not say it, and an implementer reading §5 would
discover this the same way I did.
notes:
DECIDED by Mark 2026-11-25: a new delivered-fanout table, keyed by room,
fanout sequence and destination domain, written in the transaction that
already writes the event, its outbox rows and its sequence, and pruned
on the same clock as the hub log so catch-up and retention cannot drift
(§6).

THE READINGS IN THE DESIGN ABOVE WERE WRONG, and the correction is why
this is not a one-column change. I recommended keeping one fanout body
per event before checking two things:

* NOTHING IN PRODUCTION READS room_event.bytes. The only SELECT of it is
  in a test in store/log.rs. The hub writes the column and never reads
  it, so room_event exists to be the log and catch-up is its first
  consumer.
* A FANOUT BODY DIFFERS PER DESTINATION for a handshake. hub/update.rs
  builds accepted.outbox as (domain, body) pairs: the joiner gets a
  Welcome and the other providers get the Commit, one event, different
  bytes. So a single column per event cannot answer catch-up at all,
  and the cost is per destination rather than per event -- worse than
  the "roughly doubles" I wrote.

  Application messages are identical across destinations
  (hub/submit.rs has one fanout_body for every one of them), so those
  can share a single copy and the extra storage falls mostly on
  handshakes.

NOT CHOSEN:

* Keeping delivered rows in the outbox, which has the data in exactly
  the right shape already. Rejected because the outbox would stop being
  a queue: Store::outbox_heads takes MIN(id) per (room, domain) as the
  row to attempt, so a kept row becomes the head and delivery stalls
  unless a delivered filter is threaded through every outbox query, now
  and in future.
* Serving only application messages and refusing handshake catch-up.
  Cheapest, and it contradicts the design note's own reason for
  numbering every fanout: "a follower that missed a handshake needs it
  as much as a message".

STILL MINE TO DECIDE, and defaulting to no: whether to drop
room_event.bytes now that the fanout is stored and contains the message.
The option Mark chose noted it could go. Keeping it for now, because
removing the hub's record of what it accepted is not reversible for data
already stored, and the storage is bounded by retention either way. It
becomes a sensible cleanup once something other than catch-up depends on
the new table.

Unblocks the handler of bead mimid-1wgh.37.104.3.
